title: Quantization QA: FP8/INT8 calibration and structured-output function-call JSON schema validation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Define and implement a robust calibration + validation workflow to ensure FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles do not materially degrade structured output and function-calling JSON schema adherence for our runtime models. Background: We have seen regressions in structured outputs when using aggressive quantization profiles (especially static INT8) for some models. These regressions manifest as malformed JSON, missing required fields in function calls, and subtle type errors that break downstream consumers. This ticket scopes the engineering work to build a repeatable calibration pipeline, produce per-profile accuracy metrics against a function-call / schema dataset, and integrate automated gates for releases and CI. Approach:
1) Calibration pipeline: prototype scripts that run representative prompts through the FP16 baseline to collect activation ranges and KV cache distributions. Support both per-channel and per-tensor scaling, bias correction, and outlier clipping. Store calibration artifacts as versioned calibration maps (S3 path) per model+profile.
2) Evaluation harness: create a test corpus of ~15k prompt+schema pairs focused on function calling, nested JSON, enums and edge cases (long lists, non-ASCII, numeric formatting). Implement a validator that checks: 1) JSON parse success, 2) JSON Schema conformance, 3) field-level equality checks for required fields, 4) semantic hooks (e.g., type coercion allowed only when safe). Report per-example failures and categorized failure types (parse error, schema missing field, wrong type, truncated output).
3) Metrics and thresholds: compute schema pass rate, invalid-JSON rate, field-pass-rate, mean token diffs for function call arguments. Define baseline on FP16 and target thresholds for profiles: FP8 should be within 0.5 percentage points of FP16 schema pass; INT8 within 1.5 percentage points. Absolute thresholds: schema pass >= 99.0% for FP8 and >= 98.0% for INT8 given current FP16 baseline ~99.5%.
4) CI & gating: add a GitHub Actions job `quant-schema-check` that runs on PRs that touch quantization code, model packaging, or release manifests. Nightly full-run job for all production models and profiles. Canary rollout gate: if profile fails threshold on canary model set, automatically block auto-rollout and create rollback ticket.
5) Calibration experiments: test static vs dynamic per-layer quantization, mixed FP8/INT8 profiles, and 8-bit bias-correction techniques. Track latency/cost trade-offs (tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1M tokens) alongside pass rates.
6) Automation: when a profile is validated, generate a signed calibration artifact and attach to model bundle; include metadata header `calib://...` used at runtime to pick scales.
Acceptance criteria are below and documented in a separate field. Links to datasets, draft PRs and design doc are included.
acceptance_criteria:
1) The calibration pipeline can produce a stable calibration artifact for a given model+profile and persist it to S3 with a reproducible identifier.
2) The evaluation harness runs end-to-end on the 15k prompt+schema corpus and emits a report with per-example diagnostics.
3) Measured schema pass rates: FP8 >= 99.0% and INT8 >= 98.0% (relative to current FP16 baseline ~99.5%). Invalid JSON rate <= 0.5% for FP8 and <= 1.0% for INT8. Field-level critical failures (missing required field) <= 0.2% for FP8 and <= 0.5% for INT8.
4) CI integration: `quant-schema-check` job passes for any PR that modifies quantization code; failure creates a blocking status. Nightly job publishes historical metrics to the model dashboard.
5) Canary policy: If schema pass drops by >0.5pp for FP8 or >1.0pp for INT8 vs baseline for canary models, block rollout and open a rollback ticket automatically.
6) Documentation: calibration README, how-to for running the harness locally, and an operations runbook for canary failures are checked into the infra repo and linked from the ticket.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Rohit Suresh: Prototype calibration script complete (per-tensor, per-channel flows). Verified activation range collection on small Llama2 variant. Next: add clipping/outlier logic and produce reproducible calibration maps.

2026-03-07 - Lina Zhou (QA): Collected 2k function-call prompts from telemetry (anonymized). Found early INT8 run produced 3.4% invalid JSONs on this subset, mostly due to truncated arrays in nested objects.
2026-03-09 - Rohit Suresh: Implemented bias correction patch (8-bit bias folding). Re-ran subset: invalid JSONs dropped to 0.9% for INT8. Need full corpus run to validate field-level failures.

2026-03-12 - Marcus Rivera (Runtime): Hooked up runtime to accept `calib://` artifact pointers for local testing. Observed performance regression in FP8 on A100 (kernel selection mismatch) — filed dependency ENG-7822.

2026-03-13 - Ava Martinez (PM): Confirmed metrics to surface in Console: schema_pass_rate, invalid_json_rate, critical_field_fail_rate, avg_token_delta. Please ensure dashboards include time series and model+profile breakdowns.

2026-03-14 - Rohit Suresh: Running full 15k-corpus validation across three model sizes (base, medium, large) for FP16/FP8/INT8. Early results: FP8 close to baseline on base & medium; large model shows INT8 degradation in numeric serialization tests. Will attach full report by 2026-03-16.
notes: Tradeoffs: static INT8 with tight clipping reduces cost but increases risk for structured output; per-layer mixed precision appears promising. Operationally, prefer conservative defaults and explicit opt-in for aggressive profiles until Canary gates are reliable.
